head.title: Private Chef vs Catering in Dubai: Your Private Chef vs Dubai Guide (2026) | myCHEF Dubai
head.meta_description: Private chef vs Dubai catering, explained: choose a private chef for an intimate meal cooked to order at home (about 2-12 guests, from AED 700-950 per person); choose catering to feed a crowd.
head.h1: Private Chef vs Catering in Dubai — Real Prices and Timings

opening_paragraph: A private chef is the better fit for small seated dinners; catering is built for volume. In a private chef vs Dubai catering decision, book a myCHEF private chef for an intimate meal cooked to order at home, from AED 700 per person; book catering to feed a crowd. A private chef sells the experience of a restaurant built for one table. Catering feeds a bigger room well. Everything below is that choice, explained in plain terms.

add_block.new_heading: What is the real difference between a private chef and catering?
new_paragraphs: The difference comes down to intimacy versus scale. A private chef cooks a set menu in your kitchen, plates every course and clears up afterwards, so the evening runs like a small restaurant that exists only for your guests. Catering takes that same food and stretches it across a bigger event, with a service team, warmers and often a buffet behind it. Dubai's official Food Code treats both as a food establishment, which it defines as any place where food is prepared, traded or sold to the consumer, including caterers and temporary kitchens. So the legal category is the same; the experience is not.

add_block.new_heading: How many guests before you should switch to catering?
new_paragraphs: Around twelve is the usual tipping point. One private chef can plate beautifully for roughly 2 to 12 covers before timing and hot-holding start to fight back. Beyond that you want stations, warmers and a team plating in parallel, which is catering territory. If your headcount sits right on that line, tell us the format you have in mind and we will point you to the right fit, since myCHEF runs both sides. A seated party for forty is a catering job. An anniversary dinner for six is a private chef job. Most bookings sort themselves out the moment you count heads.

add_block.new_heading: Personal chef vs private chef — not the same job
new_paragraphs: A private chef cooks the meal you are about to eat, for one household or one event, and is in the room while you eat it. A personal chef normally works across several clients, comes in for a cooking session and leaves a week of food portioned and labelled in your fridge. The two words get used interchangeably in Dubai, but they buy different things: presence at the table, or food in the fridge.

That distinction maps onto three real arrangements. A private-chef dinner is priced per head at AED 700 to 950 and exists for one evening. Personal-chef style cooking is what our weekly meal prep is — from AED 1,898 a week for 2 to 3 sessions, or AED 2,698 for a larger household at 4 to 6 — where nobody serves you and the value is in the fridge on Wednesday. A full-time placement is a third thing again, quoted per programme. If the cooking itself is the occasion, you want a private chef. If the cooking is a logistics problem you would like solved, you want the personal-chef pattern.

new_paragraphs: A live in chef dubai households ask about is a full-time placement with accommodation, and it sits outside the per-event pricing entirely. So does daily cooking without live-in: the same chef in your kitchen every day, cooking breakfast, lunch and dinner around your family's schedule. Both are quoted per programme instead of per head, because the variable is how much of the week the chef works — meals per day, days per week, live-in or travelling to you, and how often you entertain.

The useful way to choose is by frequency. One evening a month is a private-chef booking. A few structured cooking sessions a week is meal prep. Every day is a full time private chef dubai placement, and that is where a written programme quote replaces a per-person rate. Guests do not change that logic — a placement chef still steps up to cook a dinner party, at the same per-head event rates.

add_block.new_heading: Do private chefs and caterers in Dubai need the same licences?
new_paragraphs: They share one regulator, but the permit route differs. In Dubai, food safety sits with the Dubai Municipality Food Safety Department, which enforces the Dubai Food Code across every food establishment. A catering company works under a trade licence plus a food establishment permit, while cooking at a private event, classed as party cooking, needs event approval. The official Dubai Municipality permits guidance states the application is filed at least three working days before the event, with the caterer, venue and organiser registered on Dubai's FoodWatch platform. Every myCHEF chef works inside these rules, so the paperwork is not your problem.

add_block.new_heading: How do prices and menus work?
new_paragraphs: You pay a private chef per person and a caterer per event. A private chef dinner starts around AED 700 to 950 per guest and climbs with extra courses, premium ingredients and party size; a bespoke tasting menu with wine pairing starts at AED 1,400 per head. Catering is packaged instead: a drop-off spread might open near AED 2,400, a staffed buffet around AED 3,600, and a full plated event with service closer to AED 4,500 to 5,500, depending on numbers and format. Every quote is itemised, and you can compare live figures on our prices page. No two menus in Dubai are identical, so the menu drives the number, not a rate card.

add_block.new_heading: When should you book each one, and what should you plan?
new_paragraphs: Book a private chef when the night is about the experience, and catering when it is about volume. That is how to weigh the two in practice. A short planning checklist: fix the date, count guests, pick a venue, then decide between plated intimacy and a self-serve spread. For date nights, small celebrations and villa dinners, hire a private chef; for weddings, corporate functions and large parties, choose catering. add_block.new_heading: Planning either option step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your proposal arrives.
Book a private-chef dinner at least 48 hours ahead and a catering package 72 hours ahead; live stations and multi-staff events want 3 to 5 days, larger productions 7 to 14.
Confirm the menu about 7 days out, when the guest list is firm.
Ask early about allergies and dietary plates — not in the last 48 hours before the event.
Check the access route before the day — setup starts roughly 2 hours ahead.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

new_paragraphs: What is the short answer?
Choose a private chef for an intimate meal cooked to order in your home (usually 2-12 guests, from AED 700-950 per person); choose catering for a larger event with service staff, buffets or stations.
How much does a private chef cost in Dubai?

AED 950 to 1,300 per head at a table of two, AED 750 to 1,000 at six, AED 700 to 950 at ten, and from AED 600 above twenty guests. A tasting menu with wine pairing starts at AED 1,400 a head. How much it costs to hire a private chef therefore falls as the table grows, because one chef's evening is shared between more plates.
What is the difference between a personal chef and a private chef?

A private chef cooks the meal you are about to eat and is there while you eat it. A personal chef usually cooks across several clients and leaves a week of portioned food in your fridge. In our range that is a private-chef dinner from AED 700 per person versus weekly meal prep from AED 1,898.
Can I book a chef daily, or live-in?

Yes. Daily cooking and live-in placements are quoted per programme instead of per head, because the variable is how much of the week the chef works — meals per day, days worked, live-in or travelling in, and how often you entertain. Event cooking for guests is still charged at the per-person rate.
Which is cheaper for a small dinner, a private chef or a caterer?

A private chef is usually cheaper for a small dinner, because you pay a per-head rate instead of an event minimum built for a crowd. At six or eight guests that per-person figure is often better value than a catered package.
How many guests can one private chef cook for?
One private chef comfortably plates for about 2 to 12 guests. Beyond a dozen covers the timing gets hard for a single pair of hands, and you move into catering with stations and a service team.
Do I need a permit for a private chef at my villa?

No, the chef handles it. Under Dubai Municipality rules, cooking at a private event is party cooking and needs event approval, filed at least three working days before the date, so you never touch the paperwork.
Can myCHEF cook halal and special-diet menus?
Yes. Halal is standard, and Layla Hassan builds Arabic, Ramadan and iftar menus, while any menu can be adapted for vegetarian, allergy-aware and other dietary needs on request.
How do I get an exact quote?
Share your date, guest count and venue with myCHEF and you will get an itemised proposal, usually within one business day. The more detail on format and headcount, the tighter the number.
Which chef will cook at my event?
We match the cuisine to the chef: Marco Rossi for Italian and Mediterranean, Layla Hassan for Arabic and halal, Matteo Moretti for pastry and desserts, and Ahmed Al-Rashid for fine dining.

add_block.new_heading: Private chef vs Dubai catering: which one costs less?
new_paragraphs: For a small dinner a private chef usually wins on value; for a big event, catering does. A private chef is priced per head, from AED 700 to 950 per person, and independent Dubai cost guides for 2026 note that the per-person figure falls as guest numbers rise, because the chef's fixed time and travel spread across more plates. Catering is quoted by guest count and format, and a self-serve buffet is normally the most economical option per head because it needs fewer service staff. The honest rule on cost: under about a dozen guests the private chef is the sharper choice, and past that catering's price per plate slips below it.
